about.title: Calexico Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Calexico's economy runs on agriculture, cross-border trade, warehousing, and the steady flow of trucks and equipment along Rt 111 and Rt 98. That mix of heavy machinery, forklifts, loading docks, and vehicle traffic near job sites in Imperial County means workplace injuries here often involve more than just an employer. A delivery truck driver hit while unloading near Cole Road, a subcontractor's faulty scaffolding, or defective equipment from an outside manufacturer can open the door to a claim beyond standard workers' compensation. California law generally treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer, but if a third party contributed to your injury, you may have a separate path to pursue. LawProactive connects injured Calexico workers with an independent attorney, free of charge, to help figure out which claims apply and what deadlines matter.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Workplace Injury

items.title: Third-Party Claims Aren't Always Off the Table
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker can still be pursued separately. An attorney can help identify whether your situation involves a third party.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: California requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate your claim. An attorney can help you understand what's already been documented and what still needs to happen.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job after speaking up, an independent attorney can advise you on your rights.

items.question: I was hurt while driving a delivery route near Rt 111 in Calexico — is this workers' comp or something else?
items.answer: It could be both. Your employer's workers' comp likely applies, but if another driver caused the crash, that's a separate third-party claim with its own 2-year deadline. An attorney can help you sort out which path fits your situation.

items.question: My employer told me not to report my injury — what should I do?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California, and you generally have 30 days to report it to your employer. Documenting what happened and speaking with an independent attorney early can help protect your rights.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, the connection service is completely free. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.question: Can I still file a claim if crash or injury numbers in Calexico are low this year?
items.answer: Yes. Whether local crash counts are high or low in any given year doesn't affect your individual right to pursue a claim. What matters is the specific circumstances of your injury and the applicable deadlines.
